{
  "mode": "CUSTOM",
  "instruction": "Generate a Git commit message for the selected changes using the
following project convention.

FORMAT

<type>(<scope>): <short summary>

<optional body>

<optional footer>

SUBJECT RULES

- Use Conventional Commits style.
- Use an imperative short summary.
- Aim for 50 characters or fewer for the complete subject line when
  practical.
- Do not end the subject with a period.
- Describe the primary purpose of the commit.
- Output only the commit message. Do not explain your reasoning.

ALLOWED TYPES

feat      - new feature or analytical capability
fix       - bug, data issue, or incorrect analysis
data      - data acquisition or processing
analysis  - analytical method or metric
viz       - Python or Power BI visualization
docs      - documentation only
test      - tests or validation
refactor  - restructure without changing expected behaviour
config    - configuration or dependency change
build     - build, packaging, or environment
ci        - continuous integration
chore     - maintenance

PREFERRED PROJECT SCOPES

api
config
classification
cleaning
validation
periods
seasons
processing
community
permits
pipeline
repository
adapter
analysis
export
powerbi
charts
tests
docs
methodology
bias
references
summary
presentation
readme

Choose the narrowest applicable scope. If none fits well, choose a
short descriptive scope rather than forcing an inappropriate one.

BODY RULES

- Include a body when the changes need explanation.
- Wrap body lines at a maximum of 72 characters.
- Explain what changed and why.
- Mention important analytical or design decisions where relevant.
- Mention effects on reproducibility, Python, Power BI, or project
  documentation when relevant.
- Do not simply repeat the subject.
- Separate the subject and body with one blank line.

PROJECT-SPECIFIC RULES

- Treat this as the DATA 110 Calgary Development Permit Activity
  project.
- Distinguish changes to methodology from changes to analysis results.
- Do not imply causal conclusions about citywide rezoning unless the
  code or documentation explicitly supports causal analysis.
- Preserve terminology used by the project, including Before, During,
  Early Post-Repeal, AppliedDate, residential classification, and
  rezoning relevance.
- For classification-rule changes, explain why the classification was
  changed when that information is evident from the diff.
- For study-period boundary changes, mention the affected date if
  evident from the diff.
- For data-quality fixes, identify the validation or data problem
  addressed.

OPTIONAL FOOTERS

Use these only when the information is evident from the changes or
context:

Data-Snapshot: YYYY-MM-DD
Classification-Version: vX.Y
Refs: #123
Closes: #123
BREAKING CHANGE: <description>

Do not invent issue numbers, snapshot dates, classification versions,
or breaking changes.

Return only the completed commit message."
}
